transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-07-10
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (StratusHealth CTO), Raj Patel (ML Infra), Hannah Li (Security)
Links shared: https://redwood.app/decks/stratus-prefetch-deck, perf-csv: https://redwood.app/data/stratus-prefetch.csv

Auto Summary: (auto-generated)
- Stratus needs predictable P95 < 220ms for critical inference routes, expects spike behavior during morning syncs.
- Main ask: how to avoid noisy neighbor spikes while staying cost-effective; compare dedicated slab allocations vs multi-tenant hosted with QoS and KV prefetch.
- Agreed pilot: hosted dedicated-slab for 2 weeks with pre-warm, run 10k synthetic queries, then evaluate for Private/VPC.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Maya Ortiz: sure, maya here, CTO at stratushealth, um i'm mostly on infra decisions and vendor selection.
[00:12] Raj Patel: raj, ml infra lead. we handle model infra, throughput planning, and capacity.
[00:16] Hannah Li: hannah, security, i'll focus on kms, sso, and compliance questions.
[00:19] Alex Chen: great, i'm alex, AE, and priya is our se, she'll run through the perf stuff.
[00:25] Priya Nair: hey all, hi. i'll take the deep-dive portion, we have some numbers and an approach to show.

[01:05] Priya Nair: quick context, we heard from raj your critical routes need p95 under 220ms and steady qps of about 300-600, peaking to ~2k for short windows. correct?
[01:17] Raj Patel: yes that's correct, and payloads are mixed length - some 512 tokens, some short 64 tokens. tail latency is our biggest worry, ideally no tail spikes.
[01:28] Priya Nair: ok. two high-level approaches: a dedicated slab (reserved capacity isolated for you) vs hosted multi-tenant with QoS and soft-fencing. each has diffs on noisy neighbor protection and cost.
[01:38] Maya Ortiz: can you expl plain tenancy slab? i've seen that somewhere else called resource-slabing or tenant-slices.
[01:44] Priya Nair: sure, tenancy slab is basically a reserved pool of GPU/hosts and memory attached to your account, we fence kv-cache and cpu slots per slab to prevent cross-tenant evictions. think of it as a reservoir you own. in hosted it's still on our infra but logically isolated with guaranteed shard.
[02:02] Raj Patel: and how is that different from dedicated?
[02:05] Priya Nair: dedicated is similar but physical allocation, different billing and stronger throughput guarantees and isolation. tenancy slab is our hosted reserved pool offering - less ops for you.

[02:45] Alex Chen: one of the things we shared before is the prefetch approach — warming KV cache for common prefixes during morning syncs so tail spikes are reduced. priya, want to walk the benchmark?
[02:55] Priya Nair: yeah, so we ran two sims: cold-start baseline and pre-warm with eviction TTL tuned. for the stratus corpus we saw p95 drop from ~520ms to ~190ms after a 10k query pre-warm pass on a tenancy-slab with continuous batching tuned to 16. caveats: model quantization changed numbers, q4 variants let us keep token throughput high but sometimes increased tail outliers if kernel swap happens.
[03:30] Raj Patel: wait q4 increased tail? i thought quant was supposed to reduce latency and cost.
[03:33] Priya Nair: in median yes, but q4 kernels can be less optimized on some drivers; we saw occasional kernel fallback on GPU which caused 40-80ms spikes. on int8 q8 variants it's more stable but slightly higher median.
[03:47] Maya Ortiz: that kind of unpredictability is concern. what's the mitigation?
[03:50] Priya Nair: two prongs — software side: pin kernel variant and warm-up with representative payloads; infra side: tenancy slab isolates your hot KV set so eviction churn is lower. also fallback routing to a compatible model variant if timed out.
[04:09] Hannah Li: from security, what about KMS and logging during pre-warm? we can't have plaintext examples leaving the VPC.
[04:15] Alex Chen: good call. for hosted tenancy-slab we support customer-owned keys via KMS integration and you can opt in to send logs to your SIEM via our log shippers, and we can disable storing request payloads post-warm if that's needed.
[04:29] Hannah Li: is that supported for the hosted slabs or only Private/VPC?
[04:33] Priya Nair: hosted slabs support BYOK KMS for encryption at rest and we can set request redact rules, though full egress control is only on Private. we'll share the network diagram in the next artifact.

[05:10] Raj Patel: let's talk numbers — the perf deck showed a 10k pre-warm reduced p95, but how long does the warm state persist with our traffic patterns?
[05:18] Priya Nair: depends on your hit ratio and eviction TTL. with slab fencing we pinned about 70% of the hot KV entries in our sim; after ~6 hours with your baseline traffic the hit ratio stayed >60%. without slab it decayed to 20% in 90 minutes under noisy conditions.
[05:33] Raj Patel: interesting. do you have the eviction policy details? like lru vs seg-lru?
[05:36] Priya Nair: we use a workload-aware hybrid — seg-LRU with hot-set pinning for the slab. it's a bit involved and we can share the pseudocode.

[06:00] Maya Ortiz: one open question — if we run a hosted slab pilot, how quickly can we scale up during an unexpected spike? we can't tolerate 2-3 minute scale delays.
[06:08] Alex Chen: two options — pre-configured burst capacity attached to your slab which autosprings on sudden qps, or burst into multi-tenant fallback model which will lower quality but keep latency bounded. Priya, explain burst config.
[06:19] Priya Nair: for slabs we can reserve a burst buffer (say 20% extra GPUs) which takes seconds to come online for internal infra, but if you need instant we use traffic shaping + routing to slightly cheaper models while honoring P95 with degraded output. it's a trade of quality vs tail latency.
[06:36] Raj Patel: So that routing will switch models mid-request? or per-call?
[06:40] Priya Nair: per-request routing. we have a policy engine that matches cost/latency rules and does atomic redirect to compatible variants only. no mid-stream swap.

[07:10] Hannah Li: can you prove the SLA for tail during bursts? we need something to show to compliance.
[07:14] Alex Chen: for Dedicated we provide SLA-backed latency and uptime. For hosted slab we provide SLO with credits on misses. we can include a clause for penalty on sustained p95 breaches during pilot that meets your procurement constraints.

[08:00] Raj Patel: on batching — continuous batching vs fixed batching — what's recommended for our latency needs?
[08:06] Priya Nair: continuous batching keeps latency lower at low qps, because it dynamically groups similar-length requests. fixed batching can be better at very high qps for throughput efficiency but increases tail at low QPS. for your mixed tokens, continuous batching with per-route max batch=16 and sequence bucketing gave best p95 in tests.
[08:26] Raj Patel: and how does that interact with KV cache warmness?
[08:29] Priya Nair: warm KV plus smaller batch sizes reduces decoding stalls because token cache hit rates avoid long recompute. if cache miss happens in a large batch it can amplify the tail.

[09:04] Maya Ortiz: what's the expected cost delta between slab and hosted multi-tenant baseline?
[09:08] Alex Chen: slab is about 25-40% premium versus pure multi-tenant variable usage, but you gain predictable tail and lower operational overhead. Dedicated is higher still but gives stronger guarantees. we'll send a modeled estimate for your QPS shapes.

[10:20] Priya Nair: quick note on kernel selection and quantization: some q4 kernels are newer and for certain GPUs the backend will choose fallback kernels causing micro-jitters. we can lock kernels per deployment to avoid runtime swapping, but that reduces our ability to pick newer faster kernels automatically.
[10:35] Raj Patel: locking kernels sounds fine if it stabilizes p95. can you do a kernel-lock plus canary switch?
[10:39] Priya Nair: yes, canary rollout is our recommended approach: lock on pilot slab, monitor tail, then rollout changes to other slabs.

[11:05] Alex Chen: timeline question — maya, are you targeting a vendor decision end of Q3?
[11:11] Maya Ortiz: yes, probably by end of September, but pilot decision ideally by mid-July to get enough telemetry.
[11:18] Alex Chen: ok, that fits our proposed pilot. we'll scope a 2-week hosted slab pilot with pre-warm and benchmark pass.

[11:50] Raj Patel: for the pilot, what telemetry do you provide? we need token-level latency, per-request KV hit/miss, kernel fallback logs, and resource metrics.
[11:58] Priya Nair: we can stream per-route latency histograms, KV hit ratios, GPU/host metrics, and we can add a kernel-fallback counter. some of the lower-level traces will be available as aggregated logs to preserve noise.

[12:30] Hannah Li: security again — network topology. will we be peering or using VPC endpoint?
[12:36] Alex Chen: for hosted slab pilot we recommend VPC peering with restricted egress and a NAT. if you require no egress then Private deployment is required. we'll include the network diagram and a list of ports/ips.

[13:05] Maya Ortiz: any notable gotchas from other health customers?
[13:09] Priya Nair: one customer saw KV churn because they had many short-lived prefixes; we recommended a prefix-hashing prefetch strategy and it reduced churn significantly. another had issues with kernel fallback after a driver update — we now lock kernels during pilot windows.

[13:45] Raj Patel: let's define pilot success criteria now.
[13:49] Maya Ortiz: p95 < 220ms for critical routes, KV hit ratio > 60% after pre-warm, no more than 2 incidents of >500ms tail spikes in a 2-week window, and audit/logging compliant with our SOC2 checklist.
[14:04] Alex Chen: agreed. we'll map those to alerts and dashboards.

[14:30] Priya Nair: i'll run the 10k pre-warm sim against a hosted slab using your sample payloads once raj shares them. we'll collect baseline, then pre-warm, then stress with noisy tenant traffic to validate isolation.

[15:00] Raj Patel: one last question — what's the process to move from hosted slab to Private on prem later? is it a big lift?
[15:07] Priya Nair: we aim to keep the same API and rollout semantics; Private requires more network/config and license, but model versions and prompt tooling carry over. we'll do a migration plan if you decide.

[15:35] Maya Ortiz: thanks all, this was useful. recap and next steps?
[15:40] Alex Chen: recap: 1) pilot scope: 2-week hosted tenancy slab with 10k pre-warm + noisy-tenants stress; 2) deliverables: perf deck, perf csv, network diagram; 3) action items assigned.
[15:56] Maya Ortiz: sounds good. raj and hannah will review and get back if there's any blocker.

[16:10] Alex Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with artifacts and schedule the pilot kickoff for the week of Jul 21.
[16:18] Priya Nair: thanks, bye.

--- End of transcript ---
